sites.evidence_type: topology inference (C-terminal snorkel — no accessible terminus)
sites.rationale: C-terminus not extracellular (topology 'I' at residue L) and no accessible N-terminus — C-terminal snorkel presents the tag on the surface via a TM-snorkeling linker (fallback: no natively accessible terminus)

literature_notes: Five ledger lines were evaluated. L1–L4 all describe the same CALHM5-EGFP knock-in construct in which a 3×GGGGS-EGFP cassette is inserted upstream of the stop codon, placing EGFP at the C-terminus (after residue 309). The topology landmarks place residues 200–309 entirely in the INTRACELLULAR domain; the C-terminal tag therefore faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface. L3 reports a 'plasma membrane pattern of EGFP fluorescence', which confirms correct trafficking and membrane insertion but does not change the intracellular orientation of the C-terminal tag. L5 reports an HA-tagged CALHM5 expressed in HeLa cells but states no junction residue, no terminus, and no loop — the tag position is completely unstated. Under the rules, a commercial or exogenous construct whose tag position is unstated cannot be pinned to insert_after_residue and therefore does not qualify as a site. No ledger line supports an extracellular insertion at any pinnable position; zero sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal EGFP fusion (3×GGGGS linker + EGFP upstream of stop codon) is tolerated and traffics to the plasma membrane, but residue 309 lies within the intracellular domain (200–309); the tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
